snippet.textDisplay:
Been experiencing every one of the initial items you listed in start of video.....been 6 years, ever since Covid, help is super hard to hire in our area. People who have the higher level experience we need are expecting $20-25 an hour, which doesnt work well on a modest fixed income.

Agencies are up to $43/hr (confirmed last week) as opposed to $30/hr five years ago. IHSS pool of caregivers is a poor resource for outside help because they pay $19/hour, less than the $20/hr wages Gov Newsome approved at fast food places with ZERO experience required. It is a helpful program to be able to pay family caregivers who were having to quit careers in order to be available for their loved one providing all care 7 days a week, without days off.

In addition to all the things mentioned, have lost my sense of personhood and totally identify with "my needs don't matter"😢Feel like I am not able to be myself anymore.

This is a growing problem and will just get worse as next set of baby boomers retire over next 2-5 years. Thanks Mel for covering this very crucial topic in our society!!

snippet.textDisplay:
The worst part for me is when I socialize and relatives give remarkssuch as "your burdens are so heavy, I feel for you" or "you have so many responsibilities at such a young age" or "why don't you try to do this?" or "why don't you do that instead?" Yet not a single one of them actually gives a helping hand, it's hypocrisy is what it is, and you feel lonelier than ever... Sometimes I'm hating socializing because no one truly understands... Anyway, my mom has been ill for years, she recently started experiencing early dementia when she's in her 50s and I've just turned 30, I've recently cared for 3 months extensively for my grandma who had cancer and passed away, so many sleepless nights, and days of burnout and exhaustion... It's okay I can take it all, being a Christian and believing in Christ gives me strength... We all have a cross or burden to carry in life, and we ARE supposed to care for our family members, it is our duty, our responsibility, as humans we need each other's love and care...

That's why I say the worst part of it all is when some family members withdraw from helping and put an overload responsibilities on others, those are in my opinion one of the worst kinds of people

Otherwise we would all be glad and proud of caring for our loved ones no matter how ill they are... Instead we are complaining and exhausted because responsibilities are fairly distributed 💔

snippet.textDisplay: Whoosh. I was an RN for almost 40 years while raising two daughters (one of which was a challenge above all challenges and she still is), and then having to keep everything going at home because my husband was a workaholic...never home, never involved with anything. He retires and develops dementia. Guess who is his primary caregiver? He's in the moderate stage and it taking a major toll on me. I can't continue this way for much longer. I have not had a break from caregiving for literally decades. Who's caring for the caregiver? Answer: no one
